cohort: The study included 25 neonates and infants younger than 3 months of age diagnosed with bone and joint infections (BJIs) at a single institution between 2014 and 2021.
finding: Staphylococcus aureus, particularly MRSA, is the main pathogenic bacteria in BJI cases complicated with sepsis in neonates and young infants, and those with concurrent SA and OM or congenital deformities are more likely to develop sepsis.
